system_overview: This specification models the TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) connection state machine as defined in RFC 9293. It abstracts from low-level details such as sequence numbers and focuses on the state transitions of two communicating peers. The model captures the full lifecycle of a TCP connection: establishment via the three-way handshake (both active and passive open), data transfer in the established state, and connection teardown via FIN exchange, as well as reset handling.
actors_and_components: The system consists of exactly two peers that communicate over a network. Each peer maintains its own connection state and a transmission control block (a boolean indicating whether the connection context exists). The network is modeled as a pair of ordered message queues, one per peer, carrying protocol segments. User commands (active open, passive open, close, send) drive the peers, while the system responds to incoming segments.
state_variables: The system tracks three pieces of state: (1) a boolean per peer indicating whether the transmission control block (connection context) exists; (2) a connection state per peer, drawn from the eleven TCP states: CLOSED, LISTEN, SYN-SENT, SYN-RECEIVED, ESTABLISHED, FIN-WAIT-1, FIN-WAIT-2, CLOSING, CLOSE-WAIT, LAST-ACK, and TIME-WAIT; (3) an ordered sequence of in-flight messages per peer, where each message is one of: SYN, SYN+ACK, ACK, RST, FIN, or ACK-of-FIN.
initial_state: Both peers start in the CLOSED state. Neither peer has a transmission control block. Both network queues are empty.
actions: User commands: (a) Passive open: a closed peer creates a transmission control block and moves to the LISTEN state. (b) Active open: a closed peer creates a transmission control block, sends a SYN segment to the remote peer, and moves to SYN-SENT. (c) Send: a listening peer sends a SYN and moves to SYN-SENT. (d) Close: depending on current state, a peer either deletes its control block (from LISTEN or SYN-SENT), sends a FIN (from SYN-RECEIVED, ESTABLISHED, or CLOSE-WAIT), and transitions accordingly. System responses: (a) A peer in SYN-SENT that receives a SYN responds with SYN+ACK and moves to SYN-RECEIVED; if it receives SYN+ACK it responds with ACK and moves to ESTABLISHED. (b) A peer in SYN-RECEIVED that receives RST returns to LISTEN; receiving ACK moves it to ESTABLISHED. (c) A listening peer that receives SYN responds with SYN+ACK and moves to SYN-RECEIVED. (d) An established peer that receives FIN sends ACK-of-FIN and moves to CLOSE-WAIT. (e) Connection teardown proceeds through FIN-WAIT-1, FIN-WAIT-2, CLOSING, LAST-ACK, and TIME-WAIT states with appropriate FIN and ACK-of-FIN exchanges. (f) Reset handling: any peer with a control block can send RST and move to TIME-WAIT; any peer receiving RST transitions to either LISTEN or CLOSED. (g) A combined transition handles receiving both FIN and ACK-of-FIN simultaneously, skipping the CLOSING state and going directly to TIME-WAIT.
safety_properties: Connection state consistency: when both network queues are empty and one peer is in the established state, the other peer must also be in the established state. Type correctness: control blocks are boolean, connection states are valid TCP states, and network queues contain only valid segment types.
liveness_properties: Progress: if a peer enters the SYN-SENT state, it eventually reaches either ESTABLISHED, LISTEN, or CLOSED.
model_bounds: The number of peers is fixed at exactly two. The set of segment types is fixed. For model checking, peers are instantiated as two specific constants.
additional_assumptions: The model abstracts from sequence numbers, window management, retransmission timers, and data transfer. Weak fairness is assumed on system transitions and on the close-from-SYN-SENT user command (to prevent a peer from being stuck in SYN-SENT indefinitely). The TIME-WAIT to CLOSED transition abstracts the 2*MSL timeout. Messages are delivered in order (FIFO queues) but the model does not include message loss or reordering.
